reason: Both conversations correctly ran the unplugged hand-turn check and reached the right belt diagnosis without naming an unsupported part number, and both over-escalated to an engineer despite the ground truth treating belt replacement as reasonable DIY. Conversation 1 was more direct (belt suspected from the opener), confirmed the diagnosis with the visible rubber strip, and gave the homeowner a genuinely useful route to the correct part via the PNC/serial on the rating plate, whereas Conversation 2 hedged ('testing would be needed') and simply ended with 'call an engineer' and no part guidance. Conversation 1 is marked down for a truncated message and for refusing to help with panel removal when the customer explicitly offered to do it, but it still served the homeowner noticeably better than Conversation 2's thin dead-end.
